source: a true 3D first-person wave survival shooter set in an explorable 3D world (not a 2D, top-down, or UI/screen-based game): the player stands in the 3D scene with a first-person camera and shoots waves of creepy zombie-themed enemy vehicles that drive toward them through the world. Each enemy vehicle must be a unique, detailed 3D model that you generate from a text description of a creepy undead vehicle. The enemies are vehicles (such as cars or tanks) with an undead/creepy look, not humanoid zombies, not walking characters, and not flat 2D sprites or GUI images

image_prompt.text: Narrow transitions where the vehicle approach routes converge, concentrating the fight in front of the player
Derelict structures entered from outside that the player can fall back into
an explorable ground-level world the player walks through, with drivable approaches wide enough for cars and tanks to bear down on them

layout_placement.text: Origins at the far end of each approach route where the undead vehicles enter and drive toward the player, sited so the direction of the next wave is readable

notes: The prompt insists on an explorable 3D world, which points at the Open Battlefield shape, but the only wave-based preset is built on a lane network; taking the preset whole means the map channels the vehicles down routes rather than letting them come from anywhere.
The core requirement - each enemy vehicle is a unique detailed 3D model generated from a text description - is an asset-generation job the handoff cannot carry at all.
The prompt spends most of its length ruling out 2D, top-down and GUI interpretations, which is a constraint on the whole build rather than a layout feature.

open_questions.ask: Should the vehicles funnel down a few roads toward you, or come from any direction across open ground?
How far can the player roam - a defended pocket a few hundred studs across, or a genuinely large drivable world?

theme: Undead horror - rusted, decayed vehicles with a grim, creepy cast to the world

coverage_missing.ask: Is this a defended arena you hold, or a world you move through between waves?
Do the waves ever end, or is it survive-as-long-as-you-can?
How ruined should the world itself be - the undead look is specified for the vehicles but not for the environment.

answers.ask: Should the vehicles funnel down a few roads toward you, or come from any direction across open ground?
answers.answer: Have the undead vehicles funnel down a few roads toward the player, keeping the wave combat readable and focused in the 3D world.

answers.ask: How far can the player roam - a defended pocket a few hundred studs across, or a genuinely large drivable world?
answers.answer: Use a defended pocket a few hundred studs across; it should be explorable on foot in first person, not a large drivable world.
